competitor_mentions.quote: We also had a quick look at how Storsund BI handles bulk data access, mostly for context on what's typical at this end of the market.
Keeping half an eye on Storsund BI as part of general market awareness, nothing more than that for now.

narrative: An export size-limit problem was never actually answered - the account built its own API-batching workaround and stopped chasing rather than getting resolution. The underlying alert bug (failure notification not firing when the size limit hits) is explicitly waved off as "low priority" now that the workaround exists, and Storsund BI gets a casual mention in two consecutive tickets. Nothing urgent yet, but this is quiet self-sufficiency replacing reliance on the product, not health.
Single routine bug report (duplicate function failing on one template), resolved in three days. No pattern, no friction beyond the one ticket.

Steady stream of routine admin/API questions and bugs across a year, all resolved. The one recurring thread - an alert threshold that kept reverting - was chased twice ("never did hear back", "would like this properly closed out this time") but got a confirmed fix in the final ticket. Mild persistence, not anger, and it ends clean.

Active, varied ticket volume across a year (alerts, connectors, exports, dashboards) with normal turnaround. The one recurring thread - a slow-loading dashboard - was flagged, followed up once, and closed. No unresolved threads, no competitor talk, no anger.

competitor_mentions.quote: As part of next year's tooling review we've been asked to also look at Dashlume, but for now this is the platform we're on and would like it working reliably again.

narrative: Only three tickets in nine months, but the substance is concerning: the December NetSuite sync fix "didn't fully take" - dashboards resumed showing stale data in February, described by the customer as "similar to the sync issue we reported before the patch." They've quietly started refreshing manually before their 9am review rather than pushing for a real fix, and Dashlume is already named as part of a formal next-year tooling review. Low volume, polite tone, real unresolved fault - the sparse pattern the playbook warns about.
Two well-spaced, routine tickets (invite delivery, PDF export clipping), both resolved quickly. No signal of concern either way.

competitor_mentions.quote: We're currently reviewing our BI tooling for next year, and Dashlume has come up partly because of stability concerns like this one.
We're also part-way through a proof-of-concept with Dashlume as part of the same renewal review, so getting our current numbers accurate matters more than usual this time round.
Our Dashlume evaluation is ongoing and this kind of thing is exactly what we're being asked to weigh up.

narrative: Textbook quiet-risk account. A report builder rendering fault that was marked fixed in April resurfaced in August with "the fix didn't fully hold," and the team has built a permanent manual spot-check into their Monday routine rather than expect a real fix. Meanwhile Dashlume has escalated from a tooling review, to an active proof-of-concept tied to the autumn renewal, to an ongoing evaluation explicitly weighing this exact kind of recurring failure. Calm tone throughout, but every signal - recurrence, workaround, competitor POC ahead of renewal - points at cancellation risk.
Four routine, varied tickets over four months, all resolved without recurrence or complaint. Healthy, unremarkable engagement.

Export corruption reported in December was never fixed by Kataja - the customer's own April ticket notes it as "which we ended up working around ourselves," i.e. abandoned rather than resolved. Only two tickets in five months and no anger, but one real unresolved fault sitting quietly in the background.

A VP Finance account with a genuine crisis period: by December "this is the third separate issue I have raised," and by February the tone is explicit escalation - "the report builder is currently not fit for purpose," three concurrent active bugs, and a demand for "a call with someone technical this week, not a ticket that sits for six days." That specific triple-bug complaint is never explicitly confirmed fixed in later tickets. Notably, the two most recent tickets (May) are back to calm, technical, non-urgent questions with no trace of the earlier anger - the relationship appears to have weathered the storm, but the unresolved escalation thread and the VP's willingness to go straight to "not fit for purpose" language are worth monitoring at renewal.

Consistently positive, low-stakes account over sixteen months - compliments ("Really like the new drag-and-drop layout", "The daily alert digest email is great") alongside feature requests, all handled without friction. One early seat-reallocation question was left flagged unresolved with no follow-up complaint, a minor loose end rather than a sign of trouble.

Eleven tickets in under four months with visibly collapsing patience: "This is now the fifth issue we have needed to raise in two months" (August), "I am starting to keep a list" (September), and finally an explicit ask - "We have now had ten support tickets since June... Can someone senior review our account?" - followed the next day by "The MySQL connector issue from last week is still open. This is unacceptable." Two distinct faults (the MySQL connector authentication failure and a sudden, unexplained API rate-limit cut) are unresolved as the record ends. This is a relationship in active crisis, not a customer who complains but stays.

Nine months of routine questions and minor bugs, all resolved promptly, ending with the customer proactively returning to set up a second subsidiary connector - a sign of expanding, comfortable use of the product.

Ten months of routine tickets, all resolved, with one flagged-but-unconfirmed alert threshold reset that was never followed up on either side. The account ends on a distinctly positive note - proactively asking about a new connector spotted in the changelog ("Keen to set it up if so") - which reads as ongoing, engaged product use.

competitor_mentions.quote: A colleague who previously used Dashlume mentioned their export queue never had this problem, hoping this gets sorted quickly, this is dragging on.

narrative: Only three tickets across seven months, but each reports a different reliability fault (API sync, stuck export, connector auth expiry) and the team's own commentary drifts toward disengagement: "already grumbling about just pulling the numbers into Excel manually," an eleven-day export delay that prompts an unfavourable Dashlume comparison, and a connector auth failure - unresolved at the end - that went unnoticed until the numbers stopped updating. Sparse traffic with a recurring reliability theme and no resolution on the final issue.
Two brief, routine tickets (chart type availability, adding a user), both resolved quickly. No signal of concern.

A model healthy account: nine months of compliments, feature requests, and "no rush on our end" tickets, all resolved, closing with "the export scheduler has been rock solid" and "team's still very happy overall." Engaged, low-friction, growing usage.

competitor_mentions.quote: We've started benchmarking Storsund BI's API as part of a general vendor comparison this quarter, and consistency under load is one of the things we're testing for, so it'd help to understand what changed here.
We're still mid-way through the Storsund BI benchmarking and this is one of the data points we're tracking.

narrative: API timeout/rate-limit problems recur after being "fixed" - the March ticket states plainly that "the rate limit increase you applied helped for a couple of weeks but we're back to seeing the same 429s and occasional 504s." The customer has built its own exponential backoff and local cache to keep running, and is explicitly benchmarking Storsund BI's API reliability against this exact failure mode as part of a formal quarterly vendor comparison. Calm, technical tone throughout - no anger - but a genuine unresolved reliability fault tied directly to an active competitive evaluation.

An API pagination duplicate-row bug marked resolved in April is confirmed still broken in September: "our de-duplication step is still catching roughly the same number of repeats each week, so whatever's underneath wasn't fixed, just worked around." More tellingly, the account reports its own team quietly migrating away from the product - "half the team has drifted back to Excel," and by September, "more of the team has moved reporting into Excel since spring... so the API traffic on our side has dropped anyway." No anger, explicit "no need to prioritise" - but declining usage driven by an unresolved defect is one of the clearest churn signals text alone can show.

Starts with a genuine learning-curve struggle in report builder but the account works through it with the team ("appreciate the patience"), moves through steady feature requests, and ends fourteen months later with unprompted enthusiasm: "the new template library has honestly transformed how quickly we build reports now... otherwise excellent." One minor seat-count question was left unresolved with no follow-up, not a meaningful concern against this trajectory.
